newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end sharply down on baht weakness.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end sharply down on baht weakness.

text.p: Thai stocks took another heavy beating on Wednesday, closing at a 56-month low as investors continued selling on worry about the baht's sustained weakness, brokers said.
The SET index ended 11.42 points, or 1.56 percent, lower at 722.57 on 4.26 billion baht trade. The SET-50 index eased 0.97 points to 52.48.
"There was no negative rumour in the stock market other than its concern about the baht's steady fall against the dollar," a broker at United Securities said.
The dollar's strength prompted the Bank of Thailand to fix the baht/dollar midrate at a new 6-1/2 year low of 25.96 on Wednesday against 25.91 on Tuesday.
"The central bank's downward rivision of economic growth also aggravated negative sentiment," another broker at Ekkapat Finance said.

The central bank on Tuesday expected the gross domestic product to grow 6.8 percent in 1997 against its previous projection of 7.1 percent. He attributed the slower growth forecast to government budget cuts.
The central bank policy of keeping local interest rates high to defend the baht also triggered concern about commercial bank earnings this year, brokers said.
Thai Farmers Bank dipped four baht to 109, Bangkok Bank lost three to 170, and Siam Commercial Bank dropped two to 151.
Finance One retreated 2.25 to 29.50, and Advanced Info lost two to 226.
